stories.title: Nvidia's board rules out reinstating Jensen Huang, ousted as CEO amid espionage and affair scandals
stories.summary:
Jensen Huang, Nvidia's cofounder and CEO of 33 years, is out after the company investigated his affair with a woman US intelligence links to a Chinese spy plot, and the board says it won't bring him back.

- The NYT says the woman is a recruit of China's Ministry of State Security and a top executive at a Singapore AI cloud firm accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China. The relationship reportedly helped route $7.5B in Nvidia AI chips to Chinese firms
- Nvidia's board chair said on the first earnings call since Huang's resignation that the company is not considering reinstating him, despite pressure from Trump, Elon Musk, Silicon Valley executives, and some Nvidia employees
- CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Trump has said he "would not mind" Huang's return but still promotes former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a possible successor
- Huang agreed to testify before Congress, and Democrats have opened a second investigation into Nvidia's China sales and what they call Huang's "scheme" with Trump
- Nvidia stock slid on the scandal, and investors proposed a class action

stories.title: OpenAI launches a science blog, touting a GPT-6 Astra-assisted step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
stories.summary:
OpenAI launched a dedicated science blog and keeps publishing AI-generated math and science results, while trying to repair its relationship with the researchers who have to vet them.

- A new post presents a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model, which OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra helped turn into a detailed proof
- OpenAI earlier shared model results on the Kakeya conjecture, the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics, with guidance on how researchers can verify and build on them
- Its earlier dump of 377 results on GitHub fell short of guidelines set by mathematicians OpenAI had consulted, TechCrunch reported
- Twenty-five leading mathematicians signed an open letter arguing AI labs threaten their work; one told Wired of "a perception of mobster behavior"
- OpenAI's independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI guides review and communication of results, but can't slow or redirect the research
- OpenAI dropped its Caltech "Mathathon" sponsorship and is reportedly attempting the Hodge Conjecture
